scope: Resolve the stock C collation and the B-tree text_ops class from absolute selectors or an established unqualified lookup path in ordinary table and index declarations.
rules: A two-part pg_catalog selector targets the stock catalog exactly, regardless of other namespaces in the effective path.

A one-part decoded stock name resolves when pg_catalog is the first effective namespace searched for the relevant object kind. Both collation and operator-class lookup skip the current temporary namespace.
Application and explicitly numbered temporary namespaces earlier on the path cannot be dismissed without evidence. An unqualified request in that case is rejected before publication.

The compiled column, key, and emitted SQL carry the same absolute identity for admitted unqualified and qualified spellings. A fresh schema member uses the exact local table role and retains the selected stock identities.
observations: Read the physical namespace and identity of the column and index collations and text operator class from the pinned native catalogs.
Preserve table and index coordinates, byte-ordered text rows and the exact stock identities in the constructed graph and emitted SQL.
Supply differently named catalog identities in the current temporary namespace and a real earlier application namespace. Verify their existence and measure selection.
negative: An unqualified collation or class may resolve to an earlier application namespace
A differently spelled or differently qualified selector is outside the stock domain
faults: Treat the current temporary namespace as a collation or operator-class blocker
Resolve the whole declaration from a later rather than original search path
